description: Updates that CI actually exercises are automerged once it is green; the rest open a PR for a human. CI runs `make` (fmt, lint, every test including acceptance against Postgres and the live TzKT API, build) on every push.

Automerge goes through branches, not PRs: Renovate pushes a branch, CI's push trigger tests it, and Renovate fast-forwards main only if every check passed. ignoreTests stays false, so a branch with no green checks is never merged.

packageRules.description: One update for the whole workspace: the five go.mod files share dependencies (pgx in all of them), which must move together, and x/ modules tag together.
The Makefile's tool pins. make runs these tools, so a green CI has actually used the bumped version.

GitHub Actions, pinned to commit SHAs with the release in a comment. The bumped action runs in the very CI run that judges it, so the 3-day minimumReleaseAge is what guards against a compromised release here.
A major is a changelog to read, not a number to bump.
flake.lock is never automerged: CI doesn't use nix, so a green run says nothing about whether the devShell still builds or still names go_1_27.
The workspace's own modules are replace'd to local directories, so their require versions are placeholders; bumping them to the latest commit's pseudo-version would be churn with no effect.
The devcontainer isn't built in CI, so a green run says nothing about it: its feature and image updates get a PR.

The Go toolchain moves by hand. It is pinned to the exact patch in go.work, every go.mod, the Dockerfiles' golang image, the CI workflow's go-version and the flake's go_1_27, and they must agree; Renovate can't move them together. 1.27.0/1.27.1 miscounted coverage (golang/go#80974), which is why the patch is deliberate.

customManagers.description: The Makefile's *_VERSION pins: tools run with `go run pkg@version`, so their versions live beside the command rather than in go.mod.

schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A security fix opens at once rather than on Monday, but waits for a human: vulnerabilityAlerts drops minimumReleaseAge to zero, so automerging it would merge a brand-new release, the kind an attacker would publish, with no delay at all.
